text.tspan: INC-MW-010: middleware verification, validation, and evidence.
System 1 is the configured member under evaluation. System 2 is the
engineering/build/test environment and is not a product selection.
AC-MW-010-01; bounded verification of the selected Vehicle.Speed slice.

The selected contract shall preserve Vehicle.Speed [km/h] semantics, map 36 km/h to 10 m/s and 72 km/h to 20 m/s through division by 3.6, reject invalid/non-finite samples, and expose the resulting VelocityReport field to an independent observer.
AC-MW-010-02; bounded verification of integration lifecycle behavior.

The integration boundary shall make startup, initializing, operational, degraded, and shutdown behavior observable, preserve the declared transition ordering, and prevent use before required binding/readiness.
AC-MW-010-03; bounded verification of health forwarding.

Missing, stale, inconsistent, or unavailable provider/transport/consumer health shall produce an observable degraded or unavailable disposition and shall be forwarded to the application boundary without being relabeled as healthy.

A configured member startup scenario shall prove provider registration, service discovery/binding, transport readiness, adapter readiness, and ROS 2 consumer readiness in causal order before the signal is accepted.
AC-MW-010-05; validation of integration update behavior.

An update/OTA scenario shall retain pre-update and post-update identities and observations and shall detect, rather than silently accept, loss or incompatible change of the required signal, lifecycle, health, discovery, or consumer contracts.
AC-MW-010-06; validation of fault detection and containment.

Provider, binding, discovery, transport, adapter, and consumer faults shall be detected and classified at the integration boundary; non-safety middleware failure shall not create an uncontrolled emergency intervention command.
AC-MW-010-07; evidence integrity and claim-boundary criterion.

Every retained verdict shall bind the configured member, execution environment, contract identities, raw observations, and independent observer evidence. Missing target-runtime evidence shall be inconclusive or blocked, never a runtime pass.
aaos-cuttlefish-cloud-proof.yaml. This is bounded x86_64 AOSP build and
Cuttlefish boot evidence; it is not provider, transport, ROS 2, Autoware,
lifecycle, update, fault, or vehicle interoperability evidence.
Existing reference-contract and provider-neutral adapter tests support
contract and conversion claims only. They are not target-runtime proof.
Planned evidence for provider binding, deployment, discovery, transport,
ROS 2 publication, independent Autoware observation, and lifecycle/fault
GAP-MW-025: Generated/usable VSIDL binding and deployed provider behavior remain unavailable.
GAP-MW-026: Android/KVM-to-Linux/ROS 2 transport, discovery, and deployment evidence remain unavailable.
GAP-MW-027: An independent observation of /vehicle/status/velocity_status and Autoware-side provenance remains unavailable.
GAP-MW-028: Target-runtime lifecycle, update/OTA, health, and fault evidence remains unavailable.
The claim states what the configured member is asserted to realize within
the declared claim boundary. Arguments support the claim per verification
dimension. Counter-claims bound the claim where evidence is not yet
established (GAP-MW-025..028). Verification cases and evidence items
reinforce the arguments they are traced to. Planned or blocked evidence
never upgrades a verdict to pass.
CLM-MW-010-01: the configured Autoware + AndroidSDV member realizes the
Vehicle.Speed reference contract within the declared claim boundary:
signal translation semantics, lifecycle coordination, health forwarding,
startup and update coordination, and fault containment are observable,
The claim is bounded by retained, replayable, independently
observed evidence bound to the configured member, execution
environment, and contract identities. It is not target-runtime proof.
AGT-MW-010-01: argues that AC-MW-010-01 (bounded signal translation semantics) is satisfied within the claim boundary.
AGT-MW-010-02: argues that AC-MW-010-02 (observable integration lifecycle coordination) is satisfied within the claim boundary.
AGT-MW-010-03: argues that AC-MW-010-03 (health forwarding without relabeling) is satisfied within the claim boundary.
AGT-MW-010-04: argues that AC-MW-010-04 (causally ordered startup readiness) is satisfied within the claim boundary.
AGT-MW-010-05: argues that AC-MW-010-05 (update coordination with identity retention) is satisfied within the claim boundary.
AGT-MW-010-06: argues that AC-MW-010-06 (fault detection and containment) is satisfied within the claim boundary.
CCM-MW-010-01: bounds the claim for GAP-MW-025 scope (provider binding and deployed provider behavior).
CCM-MW-010-02: bounds the claim for GAP-MW-026 scope (Android/KVM-to-Linux/ROS 2 transport, discovery, deployment).
CCM-MW-010-03: bounds the claim for GAP-MW-027 scope (independent Autoware observation).
CCM-MW-010-04: bounds the claim for GAP-MW-028 scope (target-runtime lifecycle, update/OTA, health, fault).
Evidence-based assurance claims and their supporting argumentation.
Reviewers need claims, arguments, evidence, and gaps linked
in an assurance argument for the increment.
INC-MW-009: middleware variability and configured AAOS SDV member.
Product-level assembly controlled by the Phase 9 BoF and deterministic
generated platform-stack projection. The local parts compose accepted
shared assets; they do not independently choose platform variants.
MW-CONFIG-001. Configuration evidence only. The selected application and
middleware derive the adapter through D-ASSET-APPLICATION-MIDDLEWARE-ADAPTER.
Runtime support, requirement satisfaction, safety, compliance, and
interoperability are not implied by this configured-member usage.
SRC-MW-IFEX-001. COVESA IFEX is an external interface-design source.
IFEX contributes protocol-independent Property, Method, Event, and type
classification. It is not a selected VSIDL generator, generated binding,
provider, transport, ROS 2 consumer, or deployed adapter implementation.
SRC-MW-VSS-001. Current COVESA VSS Vehicle.Speed [km/h] is persistent
observable state and is therefore classified as an IFEX-informed
Property. A binding may provide change notification; this configuration
does not duplicate the state update as an independent Event.
The canonical VSS semantic source remains the source-backed

reference contracts remain the reviewed .proto and .vsidl artifacts from

Source record for the Eclipse KUKSA Databroker candidate.
This is source provenance, not a configured runtime component.
KUKSA Databroker is not selected for MW-CONFIG-001. No requirement for
multiple producers/consumers, shared VSS query/subscription, buffering,
or centralized vehicle-data policy currently justifies the additional
broker and two custom endpoint bindings.
GAP-MW-024: A valid BoF and deterministic product projection prove only
controlled configuration. They do not prove generated bindings, provider
behavior, discovery, transport, adapter deployment, ROS 2 publication,
independent Autoware observation, or retained runtime interoperability.
Reviewers need the native SysML v2 variation and variant structure
in the model to be visible for review, so that configured choices
can be checked against the feature catalogue and bill-of-features.

checked for completeness and correctness against the selected
GAP-MW-019: The Autoware ROS 2 topic and AOSP SDV transport sources are pinned, but the selected vehicle-velocity VSIDL/service-bundle schema and its generated client contract are not.
GAP-MW-020: No System 1 production adapter process, executor, runtime,
VM, or network deployment is selected. The bounded Vehicle.Speed
campaign deployment below is System 2 evidence infrastructure and must
not be read as the production deployment decision.
GAP-MW-021: The candidate AAOS SDV boundary has not been shown to satisfy the logical service responsibilities or requirements.
GAP-MW-023: The bounded campaign exercised one AAOS/Cuttlefish host and
one ROS 2 host, but no reusable or selected System 2 capability envelope
is baselined for future campaigns. The observed campaign hosts do not

GAP-MW-022: The pinned public AOSP SDV tree provides gateway, service-discovery, data-tunnel, RPC-agent, and transport interfaces, but does not provide the selected production vehicle-velocity VSIDL service bundle, FQIN, payload contract, or generated client binding. The DE4SDV reference payload and VSIDL catalog remain candidates only.
Pinned AOSP source manifest and build target for the AAOS SDV build.
Detailed repository, revision, branch, and path provenance is maintained
in the INC-MW-008 pilot source_alignment record.
Source-backed semantic definition for VSS Vehicle.Speed. This is the
canonical vehicle-speed meaning used between the AAOS contract and the
Autoware ROS 2 representation; it is not an AAOS VSIDL service contract.
VSS path: Vehicle.Speed; quantity: speed; unit: km/h.
The canonical field/unit transformation is recorded by mapping
vss-simulation-realization.yaml; this increment traces that mapping
This implementation normalizes VSS Vehicle.Speed [km/h] to a
provider-neutral longitudinal velocity [m/s]. It does not claim AAOS,
VSIDL, ROS 2, transport, deployment, or runtime interoperability.
Source-backed DE4SDV-owned reference contract and executable rehearsal.
The reference protobuf message is `VehicleSpeed` with the semantic
field `speed_kmh`; the companion VSIDL catalog identifies the
`VEHICLE_SPEED` channel. These artifacts define a reference contract
candidate, not a selected OEM or production AAOS service.
The bounded campaign proves the reference provider/observer path,
structured logcat extraction, host-side forwarding, private TCP transfer,
ROS 2 publication, and independent observation for one target execution.
It remains a development-campaign transport slice, not an OEM contract,
production deployment, or native SDV transport result.

contract. `speed_kmh` is the explicit identity mapping from COVESA VSS
`Vehicle.Speed` [km/h]. The reference protobuf also carries timestamp
and quality fields; their semantics remain outside this signal slice

slice. The type binds the current signal boundary to the reference
payload without selecting a production VSIDL service, generated
implementation exposes metadata RPCs including diagnostics declaration,
message descriptor, publication descriptor, and RPC method descriptor.

Source-backed AAOS SDV data-tunnel publication interface. It exposes

Physical adapter candidate with explicit application-side logical ports
and AAOS SDV-side service ports. The port contracts are integration
boundaries; concrete production ROS 2 topic and VSIDL schemas remain
controlled by GAP-MW-019 and GAP-MW-022 until reviewed source revisions
are pinned. The typed vehicle-speed port below is a DE4SDV reference
contract candidate, not that production binding.
Candidate physical/software integration boundary for an Autoware-to-AAOS
SDV configuration. The AAOS model is a boundary reference; no internal
implementation, deployment, or runtime claim is made.
System 2 enabling-system candidate for the AAOS source/build and
Cuttlefish attempt. The bounded campaign used an exercised instance of
this capability shape, but provider, region, quota, disk, KVM, and access
are not a reusable product or production-deployment selection.
This is deliberately separate from physicalSoftware: the two VM domains,
host-side forwarder, and private TCP boundary are System 2 evidence
infrastructure. The AAOS service bundle emits a structured logcat record;
it does not own the network socket in the accepted path because the active
guest SELinux policy restricts that service domain. The host-side forwarder
owns the private TCP connection instead.
Reference protobuf/VSIDL message published by the generated AAOS
Vehicle.Speed provider and consumed by the generated observer.
The bounded bridge accepts the VALID quality value for publication;
STALE and INVALID remain contract values rejected before publication.
Typed campaign envelope emitted by the AAOS observer. The JSON/logcat
transport adds `schema` and `clock_domain` to the provider message. The
executable JSON/protobuf/VSIDL contracts remain authoritative for exact
serialization and validation. The source timestamp remains available in
the envelope and bridge logs; the current VelocityReport evidence proves
velocity transfer, not source-timestamp propagation through ROS.
Generated AAOS Vehicle.Speed provider. The provider publishes the
reference message through the service-bundle discovery boundary.
Generated independent AAOS Vehicle.Speed observer. It receives the
provider message and emits the structured campaign envelope through
AAOS Cuttlefish guest-side provider/observer boundary. The service bundle
does not claim direct network-socket ownership.
VM-A host-side ADB/logcat extractor and forwarder. It reads the guest's
structured record and opens the private TCP connection to the ROS 2 host.
Private TCP boundary between independent campaign VM domains. This is
development/evidence transport only; it is not native SDV transport or
VM-B ingress validates the campaign envelope, applies speed_kmh / 3.6,
boundary on /vehicle/status/velocity_status. The conversion is a role-level
implementation claim; this deployment view is not a complete internal
behavior model of the executable bridge.
Independent VM-B observer of the published VelocityReport. Its
observation is separate from the ingress node's conversion and state. It
validates the published velocity and records local receipt time; it does
VM-A/System-2 campaign host containing the nested AAOS/Cuttlefish guest
VM-B/System-2 campaign host containing the ROS 2 ingress and independent
observer. It is not a System 1 vehicle compute target.
Bounded cross-domain communication path exercised by the reference
campaign: AAOS guest -> structured logcat -> VM-A host forwarder ->
private TCP -> VM-B ROS 2 ingress -> VelocityReport -> independent
observer. The deployment is evidence infrastructure, not a production
SDV deployment or a direct AAOS-service-to-ROS socket claim. The flows
establish typed boundary topology; executable forwarding and conversion
semantics remain owned by the implementation and evidence artifacts.
